A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adalina research. All 24 pages of v2 and 25 pages of v3, including Appendices A–C, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, figures and tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5, Appendix C and Figures 1–7 report original experiments comparing semi-value approximation methods using tree-based utility functions across twelve datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains the original twelve-dataset experiments and reported approximation results in Section 5, Appendix C and Figures 1–7.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same sampling distributions, adaptive shift estimation and estimator updates. The corrected paired-sampling index in Appendix A aligns the proof with the procedure already described in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same twelve datasets, Beta Shapley and weighted Banzhaf families, and positive versus signed utility scenarios. Figure 1's panel exchange does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including MSR-Banzhaf, MSR-Prob, SHAP-IQ, kernelSHAP, AME, ARM, GELS and GELS-Shapley in the benchmark comparisons. Figure 1 retains kernel, leverage and geomean sampling.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same tree configurations, utility definitions, ground-truth computation, relative-error metrics and query budgets of 1,000, 100 or 20 per player. No revised experimental setting accompanies the Figure 1 panel exchange.

E4.justification: The paired-sampling study, gamma sensitivity analysis and fixed-versus-adaptive shift comparisons in Figures 1–3 are retained. Figure 1 exchanges existing plots; no additional ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over ten random seeds with standard deviations and fix other randomness to 2026. The new theoretical bias–variance derivation does not change empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 exchanges the positive-utility plots under the MinibooNE and philippine labels, changing the relative-error curves attributed to each dataset. The underlying plots are reused, and the general positive-utility paired-sampling benefit remains. Figures 2–7 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the original proof of Theorem 4.1 and adds a direct bias–variance proof, deriving E[φ̂] = (1 - 1/T)φ, exact variance/MSE expressions and a tighter finite-sample bound. It also corrects S4 from the complement of R3 to the complement of R2 in the paired-sampling proof. These refine existing theory without changing theorem scope.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about linear-time, linear-space adaptive approximation, improved MSE, query complexity and connections to existing methods. The additional proof does not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly describes Adalina as slightly biased but asymptotically unbiased and isolates its bias contribution to MSE; v2 did not state this qualification directly. Existing qualifications about symmetry and kernelSHAP's stronger Shapley-value performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code and TreeGrad access information, scikit-learn implementations, tree counts and depths, dataset sources and reproducibility instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the connections to OFA, kernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ and regression-adjusted estimation in Appendix B.

P1.justification: v3 corrects 'Cauchy-Schwartz' to 'Cauchy-Schwarz', standardizes some mathematical notation and adds explanatory prose around the alternative proof. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 exchanges two existing top-row panels under the retained MinibooNE and philippine labels. The additional proof causes limited appendix reflow. Other figures, Table 1 and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The alternative proof modestly strengthens Theorem 4.1 through an explicit bias–variance calculation and a sharper finite-sample bound, while clarifying Adalina's bias. Minor proof corrections also improve precision. The algorithms and broad empirical conclusions remain stable. The PDFs do not establish which Figure 1 panel attribution is correct, so the exchange is not counted as a verified empirical improvement.
